This document outlines the major maintenance 
procedures P1, to be performed every five years as 
indicated by Y5 in the title block

The LP steam turbine stop valve 
is used to protect the turbine from any pressure drops. The valve is plugged by 
closing of a moving actuator on its seat.

The first draft is initiated by 
eng. Mohamed Abdel Azeem, tested by eng. Essam Darwish, revised by EDEPC inspection and quality control eng 
Samir Abd El Gilil, 
approved by general director eng. Mohamed Anan and accepted by eng. Mohamed Elsarrag 
head sector of Damietta PS.

This document accepted by eng. Samir Abd El Gilil; 
 EDEPC inspection & quality control general director, MPIS coordinator, and certified by accountant Mahmoud Soliman: 
 EDEPC admin & financial inspection & quality control's general director, and 
 supervisor of inspection & quality control's head sector.

A work permit must be issued and qualified maintenance staff should carry the 
 suitable safety category
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required
Wear safety helmets, shoes, earplug and gloves pairs etc.

Be sure that the turbine is 
 out of service and turning gear is off.

Be sure that the all 
 electrical & instrumentation cables are completely isolated.

Be sure that the fire fighting 
 system is isolated.

Isolate the valve mechanically 
 and electrically.

Be sure that the 
 oil system is completely isolated.
Complete maintenance tool set.
Spray.
Wires for lifting.
Cleaning articles.
Filler and vernier.

Dismantle the connecting pipes 
 between LP upper casing and stop / control valve block.

Disconnect all electrical 
 connections.

Disconnect all hydraulic and 
 pneumatic connections.

Mark exact position of valve 
 and actuator stem in the stem coupling to facilitate reassembly.

Measure the stroke of the 
 valve and record it.

Remove stem coupling between 
 actuator and valve stem.

Remove the actuator by the 
 crane.
Remove the nuts (21012C).

Unbolt all the bolts (21012A) 
 fix the valve body with the turbine.

Sling and lift the valve body 
 to be disassembled.

Disassemble the heat protector 
 (21043A) by unbolting the screws (21043C) and lift it.
Raise the part (21043E).
Unbolt the bolts (21042W).

Pull up the plug with the 
 bonnet.

Raise the plug from the bonnet 
 by unscrewing it.
Raise the part (21020U).
Take out the bonnet(21020N).
Raise the part (21041C).
Raise the part (21041A).

Degrease all parts of the 
 valve with non corrosive product and rags.

Clean carefully all the parts 
 with adequate products and solvents.

Clean all screws, pins and 
 nuts by solar.

Examine visually the valve 
 components for wear, cracks, deformations, foreign bodies, etc .

Change the plug, metallic 
 rings, steam seal rings and the bonnet.

Machine the valve seat 
 carefully.

Inspect the valve parts by 
 magnetic test.

Make blue test between the 
 bonnet and the seat.

Sand blast the parts of the 
 valve.

Sand blast the bolts, screws 
 and nuts of the valve.
Assemble the part (21041A).
Assemble the part (21041C).
Lock the part (21041C).
Screw the plug in the bonnet.

Insert the bonnet with the 
 plug in the valve body.
Lock the plug in the bonnet.

Make a blue test to actuate 
 the clearances between the bonnet and the seat.
Tight the screws (21042W).

Put the heat protector 
 (21043A).
Put the part (21043E).
Tight the screws (21043C).

Tight the screws (21012A) and 
 tight the nut (21012C). Use a heating plug for tightening.

Assemble the stem coupling 
 between actuator and valve stem.

Assemble the actuator and 
 tight it.

Measure and adjust the stroke 
 of the actuator.

Connect all hydraulic and 
 pneumatic connections.

Connect all electrical 
 connections.

Mantle the connecting pipes 
 between HP upper casing and stop / control valve block.

Introduction

procedures P1, to be performed every five years as
